key_insight: Strong primary prediction scores can mask poor risk calibration and variable performance across patient populations in agent-developed medical ML models.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating medical ML for real-world use requires assessing risk calibration and robustness across populations, not just predictive discrimination.
method: Introduced Auto-MD-bench with survival analysis, classification, and sequential prediction tasks.
Evaluated AIDE, AI Scientist v2, Codex, and Autoresearch against simple baseline models.
Assessed primary scores, risk calibration, and performance under population shifts.
evidence_signal: Across 15 tasks from 10 clinical datasets, with external validation across cohorts, hospitals, and time periods, the strongest agents achieved competitive primary scores but poorer calibration than simple baselines.
watch_item: Benchmark performance does not establish clinical safety; calibration and robustness require validation in intended deployment settings.
paper_title: Auto-MD-bench: Evaluating Autoresearch Agents for Real-World Medical Tasks
